The Mahalanobis-Taguchi System (MTS) is a pattern recognition method that incorporates the Mahalanobis Distance (MD) to differentiate patterns between different groups.
The MTS involves two main components: Orthogonal Array (OA) and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR).
The authors proposed the Mahalanobis Classification System (MCS) and its integrated version (IMCS) to alleviate the shortcomings of the original MTS approach.
The MCS employs Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (BPSO) and PSO/Machine Learning tools (ML) to filter out high dependable features and address the threshold determination issues, respectively.
The IMCS improved the classification performance by incorporating threshold determination as part of the feature selection process.
The IIMCS classifier is proposed to address the challenges in dealing with measurement uncertainties in the context of the Mahalanobis-Taguchi System (MTS).
The IIMCS employs a Monte Carlo method framework to propagate the measurement uncertainty into the Mahalanobis distance space and assigns an indicator to evaluate classification reliability.
The proposed IIMCS is demonstrated in an experimental case study of an equiaxed nickel alloy first-stage turbine blade, showing satisfactory performance.
The case study used 232 blades, consisting of 193 healthy and 39 defective blades.
The classification accuracy of the proposed system in the case study is 97.85%.
The reliability value of the misclassified turbine blade is -0.78.
The frequency range used in the vibration testing of turbine blades is [3, 38] kHz.
31 repeated measurements were performed on the nominal turbine blades.
The Interval Mahalanobis Distance (IMD) is used in IIMCS to provide an effective indicator for classification reliability.
The definition of classification reliability in IIMCS is a value between -1 and 1, where a positive value indicates a good classification and a negative value indicates a bad classification.
